This loan carries the added benefit that, if the borrower meets specified goals, the entire loan amount can be forgiven upon graduation. This loan is funded by the State of Texas, with repayment made to Hinson Hazelwood, the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board. Eligibility You must be a renewal student (previously awarded B-On-Time). You must be within 150 attempted hours. You must maintain a minimum 2.5 GPA. You must complete 75% of previous year’s attempted hours. You must be a Texas resident. You must have graduated from a public or accredited private high school in Texas during or after the 2002-2003 academic year. Or, you must have received an associate’s degree from an eligible institution no earlier than May 1, 2005. If not a resident, you must not have graduated from a high school prior to May 2003, and you must be the dependent of military personnel who is entitled to pay resident tuition rates. You must have completed the recommended or advanced high school curriculum. You must have not earned a bachelor's degree. You must be enrolled full-time in an undergraduate degree or certificate program at an eligible institution. You must have completed the FAFSA and be eligible to receive federal financial aid. You must have been certified by the designated school as eligible for Texas B-On-Time Student Loan. Hardships or Other Proper Causes You have the right to submit an appeal to receive your B-On-Time Loan. The request must be submitted in writing and must explain the reason for the request. Reasons that may be considered include: A showing of a severe illness or other debilitating condition that may affect academic performance; An indication that you are responsible for the care of a sick, injured, or needy person and that your provision of care may affect academic performance; and That you require less than 12 hours to complete your degree plan. A financial aid advisor or administrator will respond to the request through your NEO email account or regular mail. A copy of all correspondence will be placed in your financial aid file. Submitting an appeal does not guarantee any adjustments can or will be made. For more information about your eligibility for the loan and forgiveness requirements, please click here . Forgiven B-On-Time loans must be reported to the IRS as taxable income. NOTE: There is not a separate application for the B-On-Time Loan. Eligibility is based on the FAFSA and availability of institutional funds.
